title: test(vue-query/useQuery): wire the mock 'queryFn' into the fresh-data 'suspense' test
body:
## 🎯 Changes

The `suspense` test `should resolve immediately when stale without refetching` in `vue-query`'s `useQuery` tests created a `fetcherSpy` mock but never passed it to `useQuery` — the query used a separate inline `queryFn`. `expect(fetcherSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0)` therefore always held, so the test could not detect a refetch.

This passes the mock as the query's `queryFn` (named `queryFn`), so the assertion now checks that `suspense()` resolves without calling it. With `staleTime: 10000` and `initialData`, the data is fresh rather than stale, so the test is renamed to `should resolve immediately without refetching when the data is fresh`. A leftover commented-out line is removed.

Verified by making `suspense()`'s fresh-data branch fire an unawaited `fetchOptimistic` before resolving: the previous test still passed, while this one fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called +0 times, but got 1 times`.
